name: Murgling
body:
Murglings are an aggressive species of frogfolk distantly related to gripplis, common to swamps and rainforests. They are fiercely territorial and see themselves as superior to most other creatures.

Physical

Murglings appear to be brightly colored, humanoid tree frogs. They have large, round, black eyes and many have patterns of black spots on their skin that seem unique to each individual. They have wide heads and no discernible neck, and they walk and stand somewhat hunched, making them seem even smaller than they are. They wear little clothing and use primitive weapons and tools, but they are quite cunning and very disciplined.

Social

Murglings are arboreal, building entire settlements in the high branches of the trees they dwell in. They need both shade and proximity to water, making rainforests and forested wetlands their preferred habitats. Despite their resemblance to gripplis and boggards, murglings hate these species above all others, and will fight them to the death over territory disputes.

Murglings spend their first year as tadpoles.

They are separated into specially tended pools at this time, during which they are fed different diets to help them develop different characteristics. When the juvenile murglings emerge from these pools, they have already developed the characteristic colors of their caste.

Murgling society is rigidly organized into castes, and each murgling’s role is determined by its color. In order from lowest to highest, the castes are:

Green: Unskilled laborers.
Yellow: Artisans and skilled labor.
Orange: Soldiers and hunters.
Red: Military officers and elite warriors.
Magenta: Scholars and wizards.
Indigo: Priests.
Cyan: Tribal leaders.

A murgling normally remains in its caste for life, but some mobility is possible—in cases of valuable contributions and great deeds. A murgling’s skin color can be changed to match its new caste by the use of ritual magic and herbal compounds. Many murgling adventurers are those whose goals do not align with their current caste, and who have accepted a mission—or created one—in order to prove themselves worthy of the caste they aspire to.

All murgling continuously secrete a poisonous substance that is harmless to them but sickens their prey. Many murgling tribes make extensive use of slavery, keeping their slaves lethargic by poisoning their food supply.

Murglings are omnivorous and mostly subsist on a diet of fish, insects, and gathered fruits and nuts.

Alignment And Religion

Murglings culture is strictly regimented and militaristic, and they have a strong bent toward the Lawful alignment. Most are also Evil, having a very xenophobic and selfish view of the world that justifies their employment of cruel tactics toward other species—including wanton destruction, murder, and slavery.

Core Traits
Ability Score Modifiers Your ability score modifiers are determined by your caste [specialized]. (1)
Green: +2 Dex, +2 Con, –2 Str
Yellow: +2 Con, +2 Int, –2 Str
Orange: +2 Con, +2 Wis, –2 Str
Red: +2 Con, +2 Cha, –2 Str
Magenta: +2 Dex, +2 Int, –2 Str
Indigo: +2 Dex, +2 Wis, –2 Str
Cyan: +2 Dex, +2 Cha, –2 Str
Size As a Small creature, you have a +1 size bonus on attack rolls, a +1 size bonus to your Armor Class, a –1 size penalty to your CMB, and a +4 size bonus on Stealth checks. You must use smaller weapons than Medium creatures. As a Small creature, you occupy a space of 5 feet by 5 feet. Your reach is 5 feet. (0)
Type You are a Humanoid with the murgling subtype. (0)
Speed Your base speed is 20 feet. (–1)
Languages You begin play speaking Common and Grippli. If you have a high Intelligence score, you can choose from any of the following languages: Boggard, Catfolk, Draconic, Goblin, and Sylvan. (0)
Other Traits
Amphibious You can breathe both air and water. (2)
Bite You can make a bite attack with your sharp teeth. This is a primary natural attack that deals 1d3 damage. (2)
Climb You have a climb speed of 20 feet, and gain the +8 species bonus on Climb checks that a climb speed normally grants. (2)
Darkvision You have darkvision 60 feet. (2)
Jumper You are always considered to have a running start when making Acrobatics checks to jump. (2)
Light Sensitivity You are dazzled in areas of bright sunlight or within the radius of a daylight spell. (–1)
Poisonous (Ex) Any creature that grapples you or otherwise comes into prolonged contact with your skin must make a saving throw or be affected by your poison. (Merely striking you with an unarmed attack or natural weapon is not enough, but a creature using an ability such as grab or swallow would be affected.) A sickened creature can repeat the saving throw at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on a success. In addition, a number of times per day equal to your Constitution modifier (minimum 1), you can apply this poison to a weapon as a swift action. You can choose to make a touch attack instead of an unarmed strike, and doing so does not provoke an attack of opportunity. Multiple applications of your poison do not stack. You are immune to your own poison and that of other murglings. (3)
Murgling Poison—contact or injury; save Fortitude DC 10 + 1/2 your Hit Dice + your Constitution modifier; frequency 1/round for 6 rounds; effect sickened plus an additional effect based on your caste (see below); cure 1 save.
Green: The target is fatigued for 1 round.
Yellow: The target takes 1d2 Intelligence damage. This is a mind-affecting effect.
Orange: The target takes 1d6 acid damage. This damage is nullified if the target immerses itself in liquid or mud.
Red: The target must use a move action to jump on its next turn. If it is flying, swimming, or climbing, it can instead use this ? move action to move itself vertically (up or down). This is a mind-affecting effect.
Magenta: The target is confused for 1 round. This is a mind-affecting effect.
Indigo: The target is shaken for 1 round. This is a mind-affecting fear effect.
Cyan: The target treats all of their movement as if it were in difficult terrain for 1 round. This is a mind-affecting effect.
Water Dependency If you fail to immerse yourself in water for at least 1 hour during a day, you become fatigued. If already fatigued, you become exhausted. If already exhausted, you suffer 1d2 points of Constitution damage. You can only recover from these conditions and damage through magic or by immersing yourself in water for at least 1 hour (which removes all conditions and Constitution damage incurred from water dependency). (–1)
Total: 11 RP (advanced)
Alternate Traits
Camouflage You receive a +4 species bonus on Stealth checks in jungle and swamp terrains. This trait replaces jumper.
Dry Skin You are able to thrive in bright light and away from water for long periods of time, insulated by a protective layer of dry, warty skin. However, this outer layer is leaves you susceptible to fire attacks. You take a –2 penalty to saving throws against any spell or effect with the fire descriptor. This trait replaces light sensitivity and water dependency.
Poison Resistant You have a species bonus on saving throws against poison equal to your Hit Dice. This trait replaces poisonous.
Striped You are an extremely rare specimen of murgling who was born with not a single color skin but two. You are considered unnatural by your people, possibly even a bad omen. Choose two different castes from the list of those available to murglings; your skin is striped in those two different colors. You have a –2 penalty to Strength, and you gain a +2 bonus to two different ability scores, one of which must be chosen from each of your castes. For example, if you choose the orange and magenta castes, you gain a +2 bonus to either Con or Wis, as well as a +2 bonus to either Dex or Int. (You cannot apply these bonuses to the same ability score.) if you have the poisonous trait, your poison does not make its target sickened, but instead applies both of the special effects listed for your two castes. For example, if you choose the orange and magenta castes, your poison would make the target flat-footed and confused if it failed its save. This trait alters ability score modifiers and poisonous.
Swim You have a swim speed of 20 feet, and gain the +8 species bonus on Swim checks that a swim speed normally grants. This trait replaces climb.
Weapon Familiarity You have been trained in the use of traditional murgling weapons. You are proficient with blowguns, nets, short swords, and shortbows. This trait replaces bite.
Favored Class Bonuses
Alchemist Add +1/4 to the number of uses per day of your poisonous species trait.
Barbarian Add a +1/2 bonus to trap sense.
Bard Increase the bonus provided by your inspire competence performance by +1/6, and add +1/6 to the number of allies you can affect with your inspire greatness performance.
Bloodrager Add +1 to your total number of bloodrage rounds per day.
Cavalier Gain +1/6 of a bonus teamwork feat.
Druid Add a +1/2 bonus to your animal companion’s saving throws against poison.
Inquisitor Add +1/4 to the number of times per day you can change your most recent teamwork feat.
Kineticist Gain +1/5 of the Extra Wild Talent feat. This feat must be spent on a water-element talent.
Ranger Choose a weapon from the following list: bite, dagger, short spear, short sword, shortbow, or spear. Add +1/2 on critical hit confirmation rolls made while using that weapon (maximum bonus of +4). This bonus does not stack with Critical Focus.
Rogue Add a +1/2 bonus on Perception checks while in a jungle or swamp.
Shaman Add one spell from the druid spell list that isn’t on the shaman list to your shaman spell list. This spell must be at least one spell level lower than the highest-level shaman spell you can cast.
Skald Add +1 to your total number of raging song rounds per day.
Sorcerer Add +1/2 to your caster level when determining the range of any spells with the water descriptor.
Swashbuckler Gain a +1/3 bonus on all critical hit confirmation rolls made while using the precise strike deed (maximum bonus +5). This bonus doesn’t stack with those gained through Critical Focus and similar effects.
Witch Add one spell from the druid spell list to your familiar. This spell must be at least one spell level below the highest-level witch spell you can cast. If your familiar is ever replaced, the new familiar knows these bonus spells.
